tagline: Down in the loess cuts, on the road Grant's army took.
intro: From the Grand Gulf Military Monument on the Mississippi, the old road runs into the loess bluffs and runs through cuts where the roadbed sits ten or fifteen feet down between nearly vertical walls, lined with fern under live oaks and bald cypress hung with Spanish moss. Every grading took it down another inch. After ten miles it leaves the bluffs and keeps to the high ground some forty miles east to Raymond, two paved lanes all the way.
A Northern reporter rode it with Grant's army on May 4, 1863, past magnolias in full bloom, and called it a well-traveled thoroughfare. It is a quiet one now.

moments.title: Grand Gulf
moments.text: Named for a whirlpool the river once made against its bluff, Grand Gulf was a busy cotton port until the Mississippi changed course and left the town behind.

moments.title: Rocky Springs
moments.text: The 1837 Methodist church is all that still stands of this old Natchez Trace watering place, whose spring dried up in 1930, and the town site is open to visitors by daylight.

moments.title: Raymond
moments.text: After the battle of May 12, 1863, Union soldiers used St. Mark's Episcopal Church as a hospital, and the bloodstains can still be seen on its floor.
